sections.text:
Joseph, peace be upon him, is a noble prophet, the son of a noble prophet Jacob, and the grandson of Isaac and Abraham, peace be upon them.

Since his childhood, Joseph had extraordinary beauty and high morals, which made his father, Jacob, love him very much and distinguish him from his younger brother, Benjamin.

This clear love sparked a fire of jealousy and envy in the hearts of his ten brothers from his father, so they decided to get rid of him so that they could have their father's face.

One night, Joseph saw a strange vision; He saw eleven stars and the sun and moon prostrating to him!
Joseph told his father about the vision, and Jacob knew through the light of prophecy that his son would have great status, and warned him not to tell the vision to his brothers lest they plot a plot against him.

But Joseph's brothers had already planned their plot, so they asked their father to take Joseph with them to graze and play.

Jacob reluctantly agreed, and when they moved away from the house, they attacked the innocent Joseph, took off his shirt, and threw him into a deep, dark well (Ghayāb al-Jib).

They returned to their father crying crocodile tears, carrying Joseph's shirt stained with false blood (sheep's blood), to make him believe that the wolf had eaten him.

Jacob had great patience and sought help from God, while Joseph remained in the dark well alone, until a trade caravan headed to Egypt passed.

They sent someone to fetch water, and when he dropped his bucket, Joseph clung to it, so they were happy with him as merchandise and sold him in the markets of Egypt for a low price.

“Aziz of Egypt” (the Prime Minister) bought him for his wife, and ordered her to honor his resting place. Joseph was raised in the palaces of Egypt and became a young man of extreme beauty and strength.

Al-Aziz’s wife was fascinated by him and turned him away from himself, but Yusuf, who was raised to fear God, resisted and fled, and despite his innocence being proven, he was imprisoned to avoid scandal.

Youssef remained in prison for a few years, and he called on the prisoners to unite God, and he became famous for his accurate interpretation of dreams.

In prison, he interpreted a vision of the king’s cupbearer, and it came true when he left. Joseph asked him to mention him to the king, but the cupbearer forgot.

Years later, the king of Egypt saw a vision that frightened him: seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, seven green ears of corn and another dry one.

All of Egypt's magicians and priests were unable to explain, so the cupbearer remembered Joseph and sent him to prison.

Joseph interpreted the vision clearly: seven years of prosperity followed by seven years of drought and famine, and he devised an elaborate agricultural plan to save the country.

The king was impressed by Joseph's wisdom and knowledge, and ordered his immediate removal and official acquittal, then appointed him as minister of the earth's treasuries to manage the crisis.

The years of famine came as Joseph expected, and the famine reached Palestine, so Jacob sent his sons to Egypt to bring food.

The brothers entered upon Joseph, and he recognized them immediately, while they did not know him in his great position and royal status.

He sold them food, and with a clever trick, he asked them to bring their younger brother (Benjamin) next time to prove their sincerity.

When they returned with Benjamin, Joseph hatched a plan to place the “Sawa’ al-Mulk” (the golden drinking cup) in Benjamin’s bag to keep him with him according to their law.

Jacob was deeply saddened by the loss of Benjamin after Joseph, and his eyes turned white from crying until he lost his sight.

The brothers returned to beg Joseph, and here he revealed to them the great truth: “I am Joseph, and this is my brother. God has favored us.”

Joseph forgave his brothers with great generosity, saying: “There is no blame on you today. May God forgive you.”

He gave them his shirt to throw on his father's face so that he could regain his sight, then he ordered them to bring their entire family to Egypt.

Jacob's sight returned, and they all came to Egypt, so Joseph raised his parents to the throne, and they fell down in prostration to him (prostration of greeting and honor as was in their law).

Joseph's vision came true after years of trials. From the envy of brothers, to the well, to slavery, to the temptation of women, to prison, until he became the dear of Egypt!
The great lesson from the story of Joseph is that adversity and trials are merely milestones that make men, and that God raises up the patient and pious, and that forgiveness when able is one of the hallmarks of the prophets and the honorable.
